title: compact comparative latency & cost slate (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Short internal collateral to communicate a compact comparative snapshot of latency vs. cost across small-to-medium conversation workloads. This is intended for: product PMs, solutions engineering, and SRE reviewers. Focus is on: (1) p50/p90/p99 behavior for taily microburst patterns, (2) end-to-end per-1k-token unit cost given batching and quantization knobs, (3) simple guidance for recommending a default config for demos and low-latency tiers.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- For 2–8 turn conversations (avg 220 tokens/respond), the p50 gaps between int8-quantized and fp16 variants are small (~5–10ms), but p99 diverges more strongly when concurrency spikes occur (40–120ms extra on int8 in our setup).
- Cost-per-1k tokens: int8 reduces raw GPU inference cost by ~24–31% vs fp16 depending on batchability; end-to-end hosted cost after added router/codec overhead is ~18–25% savings.
- Recommendation: default demo config = int8 + small-batch (batch window 10ms) + KV-prefetch enabled. For enterprise low-p99 SLOs, offer fp16 fastpath and auto-fallback to fp16 for sustained microburst > 200 qps.

Benchmark setup (short):
- Date: 2028-06-12 to 2028-06-18
- Hardware: NVIDIA A800 (in-region), single model instance per run, autoscale disabled to isolate per-instance behavior
- Models: open-variant-small (base-fp16), open-variant-small-int8 (quantized offline), open-variant-medium-fp16 (control)
- Workload: synthetic conversation generator sampled from production session traces (anonymized). Two profiles: CONV_SHORT (2–4 turns, 150–300 tokens total) and CONV_MED (5–12 turns, 600–1200 tokens total). Microburst injection: 100ms spike every 30s simulating interactive client fan-in.
- Runtime: Redwood serving runtime 3.4.1, batching window tunables applied per-run.

Measurement notes:
- p50/p90/p99 measured server-side end-to-end (request received -> final chunk emitted).
- Cost accounting: tokenized output tokens + model compute time * instance unit cost + amortized slotization overhead. Does not include networking egress.
- Each datapoint is median of 5 repeated runs, 95% CI shown where relevant.

ASCII charts (compact):

1) Latency percentiles (CONV_SHORT, avg response size ~220 tokens)

Model            | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p99 (ms)
------------------------------------------------
open-small-fp16  | 28       | 62       | 138
open-small-int8  | 33       | 68       | 255  <-- p99 inflation on spike
open-medium-fp16 | 35       | 80       | 165

Observation: int8 p50 ~+5ms vs fp16 (serialization & dequant overhead), but p99 doubled in high microburst cases due to reduced headroom (queuing + kernel backpressure).

2) Cost per 1k tokens (end-to-end unit)

Model            | raw GPU $/1k toks | infra overhead % | end-to-end $/1k toks
-----------------------------------------------------------------------
open-small-fp16  | 0.48              | 14               | 0.55
open-small-int8  | 0.35              | 12               | 0.44
open-medium-fp16 | 0.72              | 15               | 0.83

Notes: raw GPU costs are computed from sampled utilization * instance-hour price; infra overhead includes routing, codec, and per-request trace passthrough. Int8 shows 23–27% raw savings but only ~18–20% end-to-end because overheads are relatively fixed.

3) Microburst sensitivity (p99 vs sustained concurrency)

Spike rate  | fp16 p99 (ms) | int8 p99 (ms) | gap (ms)
-----------------------------------------------
baseline    | 138           | 255           | 117
+short spike| 160           | 320           | 160
+sustained  | 190           | 420           | 230

Interpretation: int8 platforms have less queuing elasticity under sustained load; fallback policies or admission control needed for tight p99 SLOs.

Configuration implications / playbook bullets:
- Default demo tier: int8 + batch-window 10ms + KV-prefetch ON. Tradeoff: low unit cost, slightly higher p99 risk under artificial spike but acceptable for non-critical demos.
- Low-p99 enterprise tier: fp16 fastpath with short-circuit admission for >250 qps; consider reserving a small hot-pool (dedicated capacity) to absorb microbursts.
- Auto-fallback heuristics: monitor p99 delta trend over 60s; if int8 p99 > fp16 p99 + 80ms for 3 consecutive windows, route subsequent requests to fp16 fastpath for 30s.

Ops notes / next steps for validation:
- Run equivalent tests across 2 cloud regions to check variance from network topology.
- Expand to multi-model mixes (embedding + chat) to quantify serialization stacking cost.
- Validate with real customer demo sessions (turn-based variability higher than synthetic).

Open questions / risks (notes to reviewers):
- Are our infra overhead percentages stable across internal builds? small changes to RPC framing affect numbers.
- The int8 p99 behavior depends on the exact quantization kernel version; this draft uses offline quantization pipeline v2.3 which differs from v2.4 currently in staging.

Appendix: short reproducibility checklist
- Checkout benchmarks repo PR #221, use benchmark-config/compact-slate.yaml
- Use runtime tag release-3.4.1 and the A800 instance type image specified in README
- Run: ./run_compact_slate.sh --profile CONV_SHORT --runs 5 --warmup 120s

Callouts for collateral: add two visual slides (1) p99 sensitivity curve + recommended fallback threshold, (2) cost waterfall showing raw GPU vs infra overhead. Keep text bullets minimal; target deck length = 2 slides + speaker notes.

-- Marina (product-optimize)
